item.title: Harvest Finance hack explained
item.description: The vaults priced their shares using a Curve pool that a flash loan could nudge. Buy shares cheap, push the price back, sell them dear, repeat.

item.title: Curve pools (Vyper bug) hack explained
item.description: The pools had a reentrancy lock, but some versions of the Vyper compiler built it wrong. The lock silently did nothing.

item.title: Euler Finance hack explained
item.description: A little-used donate function let users reduce their own collateral without checking if the position was still healthy.

item.title: Mango Markets hack explained
item.description: The attacker pumped the price of a thinly traded token, used the inflated position as collateral, and borrowed everything else in the protocol.

item.title: Nomad Bridge hack explained
item.description: An upgrade made every message count as valid. Hundreds of copycats drained the bridge by copy-pasting the first attack.

item.title: Beanstalk hack explained
item.description: Voting power was counted at the moment of the vote. The attacker borrowed a huge amount with a flash loan, voted his own proposal through, and paid the loan back.

item.title: Ronin Bridge hack explained
item.description: Withdrawals needed 5 of 9 validator signatures. Attackers got 5 private keys and signed the withdrawals themselves. Nobody noticed for six days.

item.title: Wormhole hack explained
item.description: The bridge on Solana trusted a fake "signatures already verified" account, so the attacker minted 120,000 wrapped ETH backed by nothing.

item.title: Poly Network hack explained
item.description: A cross-chain message could call a privileged function and replace the keeper that approves withdrawals. The attacker made himself keeper.

item.title: Parity Multisig hack explained
item.description: A shared library contract was never initialized. Someone became its owner and destroyed it, freezing every wallet that depended on it.

item.title: The DAO hack explained
item.description: The first famous smart contract hack: a withdraw function sent ETH before updating the balance, so the attacker withdrew again and again.
